Definition: a wavering, i.e. fall; by implication, a pole (as shaking); hence, a yoke (as essentially a bent pole)
BiblicalUsage: Mot is a pole, a staff, a thing that shakes — the spies carry the cluster of grapes on a pole between two men, and the psalmist says He will not suffer thy foot to be moved, and He holds our soul in life and suffers not our feet to be moved.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the pole and the promise belong together: what men carry shakes, and what God holds does not move.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
